brief.question: Port VIDSYNC, a Linux video player that follows Audacity 4.0's timecode, to a native Windows desktop app with the same core features.
brief.purpose: The person does not code and asked for a Windows port of the app.
constraints: Keep the original values and layout
Windows integration replaces AT-SPI, XDG and X11
brief.done_when: Cargo builds on Linux, the Windows target cross-links, --screenshot writes a real 1120x720 PNG, mechanics.json matches MECHANICS.md, and rebuild_check passes.

plan.title: Confirm the existing port and its checks
plan.why: All three baseline checks passed before changes.

plan.title: Remove the Windows console window and cross-link a real .exe
plan.why: windows_subsystem = windows; PE32+ GUI x86-64 built with MinGW.

plan.title: Package the player with ffmpeg and ffprobe
plan.why: A ready-to-run Windows zip now needs no separate installs.

handoff: Windows port is complete and packaged. app/ builds on Linux (cargo test: 9 pass, cargo build --release) and cross-links to a PE32+ x86-64 Windows GUI exe with x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc 13.2. windows_subsystem=windows suppresses the console. app/dist holds VIDSYNC-1.0.0-x86_64.exe and a 77 MB ready-to-run zip with vidsync.exe + ffmpeg 9.0.2 essentials + ffprobe + licences. Rebuild_check passes 3/3 (build, screenshot 1120x720, 93 mechanics values). MECHANICS.md target hash corrected to 4c2cb950... One blocked unknown: real Windows/Audacity 4.0.2 UIA runtime verification (unk_7f20d634372a3f30) cannot be done on this Linux host. Next: run the zip on Windows with Audacity 4.0.2, confirm the UIA 'Playback position' element and green dot, and run vidsync.exe --screenshot there. Trap: do not re-add console output on Windows; the exe is GUI subsystem. If rebuilding, MinGW was staged in /tmp/opencode/mingw, which may not persist.
